newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hope of NZ consumption-led recovery quashed - NZIER.
newsitem.headline: Hope of NZ consumption-led recovery quashed - NZIER.

text.p: Postponement of tax cuts planned for 1997 had quashed hopes of a consumption-led recovery, the independent New Zealand Institute of Economic Research (NZIER) said on Monday.
"Positive signs of economic activity in this survey are few and far between," the NZIER said, adding its survey suggested an upturn was not yet under way.

In its April quarterly survey of business opinion, a net 9 percent of businesses surveyed expect the general business situation to deteriorate over the next six months against a net 8 percent who expected an improvement in the previous survey.
Confidence was lowest among South Island respondents while pessimists only marginally outweighed optimists in the upper North Island.
The survey is the first conducted since the formation of the centre-right coalition in December. The government postponed for one year a second round of tax cuts originally due in July 1997.
NZIER said the absence of tax cuts in 1997 appeared to have rendered plans to invest in plant and machinery unsustainable for many businesses, particularly merchants.
The institute said its business confidence indicator had fluctuated around zero for the past two years and that could herald a soft landing for the economy.

NZIER said business confidence had been a reliable indicator of future economic growth, leading growth by several quarters, but added, "The latest results suggest that growth will remain low in the immediate future."
Other key features of the survey included -
* manufacturers were the most pessimistic sector
* builders' confidence fell sharply over the March quarter
* Merchants' sales remained static but orders improved
* service firms were most confident about the outlook
* finance firms in the service sector were most optimistic.
NZIER said an economy-wide weakening of prices and persistent cost increases contributed to a further decline in profits.
With the exception of service firms, all sectors anticipated further reductions in profitability over the next three months.
Reduced profits have also lowered employment prospects and intentions.
